clue.text: Something puzzling about United Kingdom displacing old during withdrawal

indicators.note: about here signals that the finished string is turned round and read the other way
displacing says one piece takes the place of another inside the word for withdrawal

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure or withdrawal
ex- as a prefix means former or old

explanation.surface: Something baffling is going on with Britain's exit, the old order replaced during the withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displacing' puts UK where EX stood in EXODUS, giving UKODUS; 'about' then reads that backwards. 'during' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The number-placement grid puzzle is literally a puzzle, so it is something puzzling.

clue.text: Dangerous water feature some plumber grouts

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tradesman's grouting has created a hazardous feature in a water garden.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg floating at sea is a famous danger to shipping, a feature of polar waters.

clue.text: Court department turns up record and reveals paper's source

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: turns says the little word up is flipped round to read the other way

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A court official turns up a document that shows where the newspaper's story came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' flips UP to PU. 'Court' looks like a law court but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed wood fibre is the raw material from which most paper is made.

clue.text: Way to absorb God — Sam worships regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of the words God Sam worships

explanation.surface: A man called Sam faithfully worships God, a spiritual way of soaking things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmosis is how liquids pass through a membrane, and figuratively a way of absorbing knowledge gradually.

clue.text: Beaten and buried in back garden, naturally

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
buried in says the letters lie concealed within the words garden, naturally

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something has been beaten and then buried in the back garden, as nature intended.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Beaten and buried' as the definition and left the hiding signal out; 'buried in' is the signal, so only 'Beaten' defines and 'and' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To tan someone's hide is slang for thrashing them, so tanned can mean beaten.

clue.text: With no hint of mask, Trump's riddled with COVID 19, ultimately getting rich

indicators.note: riddled with suggests a body shot through and disordered, so the letters are jumbled
with no says a letter is taken away from the name

parts.note: Donald Trump, taken as his name

indicators.note: a hint of a word is just its opening letter
ultimately points to the final letter of the entry referred to

parts.note: the solution to clue 19 down, the follower in that clue

explanation.surface: An unmasked president catches COVID yet still ends up a wealthy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no hint of mask' removes M from TRUMP; 'riddled with' jumbles TRUP and COVID into PRODUCTIV; 'ultimately' takes E, the last letter of 19 down's answer ACOLYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich soil or a rich seam is fertile and yields plenty, just as productive land does.

clue.text: Arsenic classified as 'miscellaneous'

parts.note: As is the chemical symbol for arsenic
things classified have been sorted into groups

explanation.surface: A poison filed under the heading of odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An assorted collection is a mixed bag of various kinds, exactly a miscellaneous one.

clue.text: Posh amongst 26 on clumsy ship — it's bumpy

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means coming after the boat

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: amongst says the posh letter sits among the letters of the god

parts.note: the solution to clue 26 down, the god of love
U is the old shorthand for upper-class, posh usage

explanation.surface: An upper-class lover travels aboard a lumbering vessel on a rough crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posh' looks like an adjective for the ship but supplies U; '26' points to the answer of 26 down. In an across answer 'on' means following.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuberous means swollen into knobbly tubers, so a tuberous root is lumpy and uneven.

clue.text: Stop a bishop with half-cut priest

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title abbreviation for a bishop

indicators.note: half-cut means only the latter half of the word priest is kept

explanation.surface: A bishop tries to halt a tipsy clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it keeps the last half, EST, of PRIEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrest a process or decline is to halt it, a formal synonym for stop.

clue.text: Mired in a smelly problem with egg flip — drink's first ingredient not working

parts.note: BO is body odour, a smelly problem

indicators.note: flip says the word egg is turned over, back to front
first ingredient means the opening letter of the word

parts.note: a system that is down is not working

explanation.surface: Someone is stuck with a stinky egg-flip cocktail whose main ingredient has failed.
explanation.walkthrough: An egg flip is a real drink, but 'flip' reverses EGG to GGE. 'in' merely links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be mired is to be stuck in mud, and figuratively stuck in difficulties.

clue.text: Sack medic before surgery

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A doctor is fired just before performing an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop someone from a team or job is to dismiss them, as to sack does.

clue.text: Heard you are invested in escort agency

indicators.note: invested in says one piece is placed inside the other, like money put into a business

parts.note: a beau is a male companion or escort

indicators.note: heard says the words are taken by their sound, as in texting shorthand

parts.note: said out loud, these two words sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Rumour has it you've put money into an escort agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is an office or organisation providing a service, such as an employment or news agency.

clue.text: Madden and mischievously pester a former associate at the start

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner

indicators.note: at the start means only the opening letter of associate is used
mischievously suggests playful disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: To infuriate someone, cheekily badger an old colleague right from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mischievously' rearranges only 'pester a'; the former associate pieces come first, as 'at the start' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To madden is to drive someone furious, just as to exasperate is to irritate intensely.

clue.text: Signal Corps invading eastern country before Lawrence

indicators.note: invading says the corps letter forces its way into the country

parts.note: India is a country in the East
C is an abbreviation for Corps
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, by his initials

explanation.surface: A signals regiment invades an Eastern nation ahead of Lawrence of Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal Corps' reads as one military unit, but 'Signal' is the definition and 'Corps' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: To signal something is to point to it or show it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Disorganised secret agent receiving discharge

indicators.note: receiving says the agent's word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
crap is a crude word for bodily discharge

explanation.surface: A shambolic spy is given his discharge papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrappy work is untidy and fragmentary, lacking order, so disorganised.

clue.text: Half-heartedly embarrass Catholic in Church Trust

indicators.note: half-heartedly means losing half of the doubled letters at the word's heart

parts.note: to redden someone is to make them blush, to embarrass them
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A lukewarm attempt to shame a Catholic during a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: REDDEN has DD at its heart; 'Half-heartedly' drops one D to leave REDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving credence to a story means believing it, so credence is trust or belief.

clue.text: Relaxes German and secures victory — success at last

indicators.note: secures says the German word holds the victory word inside it

parts.note: und is the German word for and
a win is a victory

indicators.note: at last means the final letter of success

explanation.surface: A German player who clinches a win finally achieves success and takes it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German' looks like a nationality alone; it combines with 'and' to give UND.
explanation.definitionFit: A person unwinds by easing off and letting tension go, which is how one relaxes.

clue.text: Two artists stand back to back on hill, first is closer to Penn & Teller

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means sitting above the hill
the closer to a word is its final letter, here of Penn

parts.words: Two artists stand back to back
parts.note: an artist is an RA, a Royal Academician; two of them back to back face apart, AR then RA
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A tale of two artists on a hilltop, starting with the magicians Penn and Teller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penn & Teller' reads as the magic act, but only Penn supplies N and Teller is the definition. 'first is' places N first.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of a story is the one who recounts it, a storyteller.

clue.text: Follower recycled tea-cosy — section becoming gilet essentially

indicators.note: recycled says the letters of tea-cosy are made into something new
becoming says one letter turns into another
essentially points to the middle letter, the essence of the word gilet

explanation.surface: A thrifty crafter recycles a tea-cosy, part of it turning into a gilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' swaps the S of TEACOSY for L, the middle letter of GILET, giving TEACOLY; 'recycled' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or devoted adherent, someone who follows a leader.

clue.text: High-handed op-eds blasted jerk

indicators.note: blasted suggests something blown apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: Opinion pieces have slammed some fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' reads as an insult for a person but means a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: High-handed behaviour is overbearing and autocratic, the way a tyrant acts.

clue.text: Correct film certificate

parts.note: a tick marks something as correct
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A cinema rating, appropriately awarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film certificate' looks like one phrase for a rating like PG, but 'film' gives ET and 'certificate' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket can be a licence or qualification document, as a pilot's or master's ticket.

clue.text: Engineers free up joint

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: up here means stirred up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Army engineers release a marijuana cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is used as stirred up or in disarray, rearranging FREE into EFER.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is a cannabis cigarette, which in slang is also called a joint.

clue.text: Paint coat of eggshell around handle

indicators.note: around says those outer letters enclose the other piece
the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying a coat of eggshell paint around a door handle.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggshell is a paint finish, so the surface stays in the decorator's shop; here it just gives E and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy paint that dries hard, so it is a type of paint.

clue.text: Suffer to be productive

definitions.meaning: to put up with or endure something
to yield or produce, as a tree does fruit

explanation.definitionFit: One can bear pain, enduring it, and a tree can bear fruit, producing it.

clue.text: Security firm fifty-fifty about dead gunmen

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: about says the pair of fifties surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them
the late someone is a dead person
RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners

explanation.surface: A security company splits evenly over gunmen killed on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifty-fifty' looks like an even split but is two Roman fifties. RA, the Royal Artillery, is the usual crossword source of gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Collateral is property pledged as security against a loan.

clue.text: Upset angry God

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: sore is informal for angry

explanation.surface: A deity is upset and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love.

clue.text: Special case to carry the blade

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A particular holder made to transport the knife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case to carry' reads as a holder for the blade; 'case' instead takes the outside letters of 'carry', CY.
explanation.definitionFit: A scythe is a long curved blade on a pole used for mowing.

clue.text: 24's cast won't sleep inside

definitions.note: 24's stands for 24 is, the number defined

indicators.note: inside says the sleep word goes within the jumbled letters
cast in the sense of thrown into new shapes, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to doze is to sleep lightly

explanation.surface: The cast of the TV show 24 refuse to nod off during filming.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' looks like the thriller series, but is just the number defined; '24's' reads as '24 is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two dozen is twice twelve, which makes twenty-four.
